summary: The ANSIBLE_DISPLAY_TRACEBACK environment variable controls when tracebacks are shown for errors, warnings and deprecations, with options always, never, error, warning and deprecated that can be comma-combined.
questions: How do I show Python tracebacks for Ansible errors?
Can I get a traceback for a deprecation warning?

answer_card.title: Display tracebacks with ANSIBLE_DISPLAY_TRACEBACK
answer_card.answer_md:
Previously tracebacks were only sometimes shown with `-vvv`, and only for errors. Now set `ANSIBLE_DISPLAY_TRACEBACK` to collect tracebacks for exceptions and for the call site of errors, warnings and deprecations (even in module code):

- `always`: always show (overrides others)
- `never`: never show (overrides others)
- `error`: show for errors
- `warning`: show for non-deprecation warnings
- `deprecated`: show for deprecation warnings

Combine options with commas, for example `ANSIBLE_DISPLAY_TRACEBACK=error,warning`.
